headline: Amazon Raises Starting Pay to $20/Hour for U.S. Operations Workers
meta_description: Amazon invests $1.5 billion to raise minimum starting pay for full-time U.S. operations workers to $20/hour and expands grocery discounts.
summary_short: Amazon is investing over $1.5 billion to boost pay for its U.S. operations workforce while rolling out new grocery benefits for all employees.
body:
Amazon is raising the minimum starting wage for full-time U.S. operations workers to $20 an hour, backed by a company investment of more than $1.5 billion in higher pay across the workforce.

The wage increase reflects growing pressure on large employers to offer competitive compensation as workers reassess job opportunities. The $20 starting rate applies to full-time roles in Amazon's operations division—the division that handles warehouses, fulfillment centers, and logistics operations.

Beyond wage increases, Amazon is extending new grocery discounts to all U.S. employees, expanding benefits beyond its operations workers. The dual investment signals the company's effort to improve both compensation and employee perks during a time when retention and recruitment remain central to business operations.
quick_facts: $20/hour minimum starting wage for full-time U.S. operations workers
$1.5 billion investment in higher pay across the workforce
New grocery discounts extended to all U.S. employees
Changes apply to Amazon's U.S. operations division
